parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, documented police/border targeting, facility ban, or current trans violence is recorded; courts have repeatedly protected decriminalisation, organisation registration and gender recognition, showing functioning recourse. Risks are secondary and incomplete: Section 167 for same-sex women remains unrepealed, societal discrimination and mixed official signals are documented, tolerance is only 50%, implementation of precedents is reported unsatisfactory, and traveller-facing border, facilities, custody and care rules are undocumented with violence data only from 2011. This sits above documented administrative-exposure cases but below jurisdictions with working traveller protections.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No foreign-document, X-marker or mismatch practice for visitors is recorded.
entry_documents.protection: 2017 rulings required recognition of gender identity on domestic IDs; resident-facing climate signal only, not a visitor right.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor uses home passport; dossier does not show officials doubting foreign documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No trans-specific arrest, detention or custody-placement practice is recorded.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: High court and appeal courts upheld constitutional limits on private-life intrusion in 2019-2021.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No documented path from document mismatch to detention or birth-sex custody for visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, ward or other facility-access rule for visitors is recorded.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No visitor care, medication or ward-placement practice is recorded.
care_services.protection: Community organisation provides sexual-health/HIV work for residents; no visitor care guarantee documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Section 167 covering same-sex conduct between women declined repeal in 2023, status after 2019 ruling unresolved; secondary tangential signal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Section 164 sodomy provisions struck down 2019, upheld 2021, formally deleted 2026; former police non-targeting instruction reported 2011.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Latent statute could in principle be used as lever, but no documented use against trans visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No age-dependent visitor, schooling, care or guardianship rule is recorded.
minors_guardians.interaction: No partnership recognition for same-sex couples; visitor-specific consequence not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2011 report recorded societal discrimination; 2011 deputy-speaker threat and mixed later official signals. No current trans-specific violence rate documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2011 report found no reported orientation/identity violence that year; that old finding is not current safety evidence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Tolerance 50% for homosexual neighbour in 2021 is LGBT-wide, not trans-specific, and predates present period.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: May 2024 assessment: implementation of landmark precedents has not been satisfactory; current enforcement for trans visitors unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts ordered organisation registration, decriminalisation and ID recognition; employment ban on sexual-orientation discrimination since 2010, GI coverage not documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper/court protections exist but documented implementation gap limits weight; absence of current data is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.55-B has documented extended secondary screening, missed connections and discretionary refusal. This dossier documents no such traveller-facing screening, so it sits higher.

0.65-A has explicit national equality protection, a working complaint board with apology/compensation, and brief detention ending in release. This case has court protections but unsatisfactory implementation and no documented traveller remedy, so lower.
0.75-C documents accepted matching passports, trained officers, counsel and compensation for unlawful holding. No equivalent visitor-facing border protection is documented here, so materially lower.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is formally decriminalised for the main sodomy provision and courts have intervened protectively, but protection is litigation-driven, implementation is reported unsatisfactory, and Section 167 remains a latent secondary risk. No tier-1 universal exposure or organised targeting is documented, which keeps the rating above the 0.55 administrative-exposure pattern. Conversely, documented societal discrimination, only moderate tolerance, mixed official rhetoric, and absence of current traveller-facing safeguards for documents, facilities, care and custody prevent a higher rating. Uncertainty is high because violence and enforcement data are dated or absent.
